author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Kimberly-Clark is preparing concessions aimed at addressing European Union antitrust concerns over its planned $40 billion acquisition of Kenvue, Reuters reported Monday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The European Commission is expected to outline its concerns this week. The commission’s preliminary review is scheduled to end Sept. 29, after which the deal could move into a longer investigation that may last about four months.

The companies have not disclosed a final remedy package. Kimberly-Clark’s proposed purchase of Kenvue would combine major consumer-health and personal-care brands, making regulatory review important in markets where the businesses overlap.

Shares of both companies rose more than 2% in early trading, according to Reuters, as investors assessed the possibility that concessions could keep the transaction on track. Australia and South Africa have already granted conditional clearances that require divestitures.
The report remains subject to further verified updates as officials continue reviewing the circumstances.

headline: Kimberly-Clark prepares concessions to win EU approval for Kenvue deal
